All candidates are E0 failure-point hypotheses. The journeys.json _comment names a ground-truth.json; it was not opened.

strengths.title: Draught field names its unit and explains the term ('Draught in metres', 'The depth of water your boat needs to float'), so the persona enters 1.5 without hesitation
Review page states 'You pay at the harbour office when you arrive. Nothing is charged online.' and itemises the total, so confirming feels safe
Berths page restates date, time and nights at the top, confirming the previous step

candidates.title: Arrival-time options carry no time zone while the only tide data is in UTC, below the button
candidates.description: To pick an arrival time inside the sill-gate window, a first-time skipper needs the times in the selector and the tide times on one stated basis. On / the 'Arrival time' select lists bare hours 06:00-21:00 with no time zone. The 'Tide times' table, captioned 'High water at the quay, times in UTC', and the rule 'The sill gate is open from about two hours before high water until two hours after' sit below the Check berths button, out of view at 375 px. On 17 October the UK is on BST, so the persona would have to scroll, convert UTC to local and add the two-hour margins by hand, without knowing which zone the selector uses.
candidates.impact: A visiting skipper may choose a time on the wrong zone basis and could arrive an hour off the window, at a harbour that can only be entered around high water.

candidates.recommendation: State the zone on both (for example 'local time, BST') and show the gate-open window for the chosen date next to the arrival-time field.

candidates.title: Choosing an arrival time when the sill gate is shut gives no feedback
candidates.description: After choosing an arrival time, the persona needs to see whether the harbour can be entered then. Choosing 08:00 on Saturday 17 October (high water 02:08 and 14:32 UTC, so the gate is shut) and pressing Check berths goes straight to 'Choose a pontoon space' with 'Arriving on Saturday 17 October 2026 at 08:00' and no warning. For the correct 15:00 there is likewise no confirmation that the gate is open.
candidates.impact: A skipper may book an arrival time at which the boat cannot get over the sill, and learn this only on arrival.

candidates.title: Which boat length counts is not stated, on the berth limits or on the Length field
candidates.description: A skipper with a bowsprit has two lengths (10.4 m overall, 9.6 m hull) and needs to know which one the harbour uses. On /berths.html the cards say 'Boats up to 10 metres' / 'up to 12 metres' without saying length overall. On /boat.html the field is labelled just 'Length', with no unit and no hint, while the next field reads 'Draught in metres' with a hint. Probes show the consequence: with Pontoon B, berth 14, a Length of 9.6 is accepted and priced at £61.44, while 10.4 is stopped.
candidates.impact: A first-time skipper may pick the cheaper 10-metre berth and enter hull length, booking a berth the boat may not fit, or may hit an unexplained stop.

candidates.title: 'Booking stopped' page gives no reason and no way to choose another berth
candidates.description: When a boat exceeds the chosen berth, the skipper needs to be told why and offered a way back. After choosing Pontoon B, berth 14 and entering Length 10.4, Continue leads to H1 'Booking stopped' with only 'This booking cannot continue. Reference BK-409.' There is no mention of length, no suggested berth and no link back to the berth list; only the site navigation and the office phone number remain.
candidates.impact: A skipper who made the step-5 choice may not understand what went wrong and may have to phone the office (open 08:00-20:00) or start again, which is hard with one hand on a tiller line and patchy data.

candidates.title: Confirmation omits the arrival time and the gate window
candidates.description: The persona's goal is a berth for the afternoon tide, so the confirmation should restate the tide-dependent part of the plan. The review page shows 'Saturday 17 October 2026 at 15:00', but /confirmed.html shows 'Arrival: Saturday 17 October 2026' with no time, and nothing about when the sill gate is open, although the review page promised a text 'if the gate times change'.
candidates.impact: A skipper may be unsure their arrival time was recorded and still has no gate window to plan the passage against.
